claims.claim: Russia released 74-year-old American Stephen Hubbard during Witkoff's talks with Putin in St. Petersburg.
claims.episode_span: released retired American teacher Stephen Hubbard, 74, from custody
claims.source_title: Russia frees US citizen Stephen Hubbard, state media reports
claims.supporting_quote: President Vladimir Putin says Russia has agreed to release a 74-year-old American citizen who was jailed for allegedly fighting on behalf of Ukraine, state media is reporting.

claims.claim: Hubbard was sentenced to almost seven years in a penal colony in 2024.
claims.episode_span: sentenced in 2024 to nearly seven years
claims.source_title: Russia frees US citizen Stephen Hubbard, state media reports
claims.supporting_quote: Hubbard, a former teacher originally from Michigan, was sentenced to almost seven years in a penal colony in 2024.

claims.claim: Witkoff said there is a foundation upon which a ceasefire in Ukraine can be built.
claims.episode_span: a foundation exists on which a Ukraine ceasefire can be built
claims.source_title: Witkoff Meets Putin In St. Petersburg: Foundation For Ukraine Ceasefire Exists
claims.supporting_quote: He also declared: "There is a foundation upon which a ceasefire in Ukraine can be built," in the most optimistic American public statement on Ukraine since the conflict entered its current phase.

claims.claim: Putin said the first diesel shipment under the U.S. deal will leave in two to three days.
claims.episode_span: the first shipment under this month's diesel export deal with the United States leaves in two to three days
claims.source_title: Russia frees US citizen Stephen Hubbard, state media reports
claims.supporting_quote: The first shipment under the agreement will leave Russia "in two to three days", Putin said during the meeting, as quoted by state news agency TASS.

claims.claim: Kenya has confirmed nine Ebola cases, its first outbreak, all linked to a patient who travelled from DR Congo.
claims.episode_span: nine confirmed cases all linked to a man who travelled from the Democratic Republic of Congo
claims.source_title: Is Ebola under control in Kenya after nine cases confirmed?
claims.supporting_quote: Nine cases have now been confirmed including its first patient, who travelled from DR Congo and died two weeks ago.

claims.claim: More than 4,000 people have died in the DR Congo Ebola outbreak confirmed in May, with more than 9,500 cases.
claims.episode_span: more than 9,500 cases in Congo since May, and more than 4,000 deaths
claims.source_title: Is Ebola under control in Kenya after nine cases confirmed?
claims.supporting_quote: More than 4,000 people have died since Ebola was confirmed in DR Congo in May, making it the second most deadly outbreak of the disease.

claims.claim: 134 of 135 contacts of Kenya's first Ebola patient remain in quarantine.
claims.episode_span: Of 135 listed contacts of the first patient, 134 remain in quarantine
claims.source_title: Is Ebola under control in Kenya after nine cases confirmed?
claims.supporting_quote: In Kenya, 134 out of 135 people listed as contacts of the first patient remain in quarantine.

claims.claim: Kpler data showed regional oil exports over 24 million barrels a day in the week ending October 18, versus 23.3 million before the war.
claims.episode_span: over 24 million barrels a day in the week ending October 18, compared with 23.3 million before the war
claims.source_title: Wall Street Journal: Regional Oil Exports Exceed Pre-War Levels
claims.supporting_quote: According to the report, published on Tuesday, October 20, data from the vessel-tracking firm Kpler shows that regional oil exports reached over 24 million barrels per day in the week ending October 18. Before the war, this figure stood at 23.3 million barrels per day.

claims.claim: Oil transiting the Strait of Hormuz reached about 14 million barrels a day, 82 percent of previous levels.
claims.episode_span: about 14 million barrels a day, 82 percent of the previous volume
claims.source_title: Wall Street Journal: Regional Oil Exports Exceed Pre-War Levels
claims.supporting_quote: The volume of oil transiting this waterway has reached approximately 14 million barrels per day, which equates to 82 percent of previous levels.

claims.episode_span: gas will reach homes and businesses from the end of the month
claims.source_title: UK approves Jackdaw gasfield in North Sea
claims.supporting_quote: The Jackdaw field will start supplying gas to homes and businesses from the end of the month, the government said after approving the scheme.

claims.episode_span: the field will create 27 jobs and secure 273
claims.source_title: UK approves Jackdaw gasfield in North Sea
claims.supporting_quote: When asked to clarify how many jobs the gasfield would create, Fahnbulleh said: “It will create 27 jobs. It will secure 273 jobs.

claims.episode_span: more than 12,000 ICE arrests in July, almost double Florida or California

claims.supporting_quote: More than 12,000 in July alone , almost double the number in the next most affected states, Florida and California.

claims.supporting_quote: South Sudan authorities say Sudan's army launched drone attack on market, as MSF says it is treating 20 wounded people.

claims.claim: A New York Times analysis and USGS data indicate Venezuela's official earthquake death toll of 6,509 is probably a severe undercount.
claims.episode_span: Venezuela's official toll of 6,509 deaths from June's earthquakes is probably a severe undercount

claims.claim: Giorgia Meloni announced deployment of 500 troops to Milan and cabinet measures to ease detention of minors and fine their parents.
claims.episode_span: Italy will deploy 500 troops to Milan, and Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said ministers eased minors' detention and will fine parents for damage
claims.source_title: Italy deploys army and approves tougher anti-riot laws after violence
claims.supporting_quote: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni on Tuesday announced the deployment of 500 troops to Milan to assist police following clashes in the city. Meloni said a cabinet meeting also approved measures to make the detention of minors easier and to impose fines on their parents for any damage.
